title: Ezekiel's Vision and Commission
summary: By the river Chebar in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile Ezekiel sees a storm cloud with four living creatures, each with four faces, and wheels within wheels, above a firmament with a throne and a figure like a man, surrounded by brightness. He falls on his face. The LORD sends him to a rebellious people, gives him a scroll to eat that is sweet as honey, and appoints him a watchman. His tongue is made silent except when God speaks.

title: Sign Acts of the Siege
summary: God tells Ezekiel to draw Jerusalem on a clay tile and set up a siege against it, then to lie on his left side for 390 days, bearing Israel's guilt, and on his right side for forty days for Judah's. He eats measured bread baked over dung and drinks measured water, as a sign of siege famine. He shaves his head and beard, weighs the hair, and burns a third, strikes a third with a sword, and scatters a third to the wind, with a few strands kept.

title: The Glory Leaves the Temple
summary: In the sixth year, as elders sit before him, Ezekiel is lifted by the Spirit to Jerusalem and shown idolatrous images, elders offering incense, women weeping for Tammuz, and men worshiping the sun at the temple door. Six executioners and a man in linen mark the faithful, and the glory of the LORD leaves the temple and the city. The LORD promises to gather the exiles and give them one heart and a new spirit, replacing the heart of stone with a heart of flesh.

title: The Death of Ezekiel's Wife
summary: The LORD tells Ezekiel that the desire of his eyes, his wife, will be taken from him with a stroke, and that he is not to mourn aloud, weep, or eat the bread of mourners. Ezekiel speaks to the people in the morning, his wife dies in the evening, and he does as commanded. When the people ask what this means, he tells them the sanctuary, the pride of their power, will be profaned, and they too will not mourn. A fugitive will come, and Ezekiel's silence will end.

title: The Valley of Dry Bones
summary: The hand of the LORD sets Ezekiel in a valley full of very dry bones and asks whether these bones can live. At Ezekiel's prophecy the bones come together, sinews and flesh cover them, and breath enters them so that they stand as a great army. The LORD says the bones are the whole house of Israel, who say their hope is lost, and promises to open their graves and bring them to their land. Ezekiel joins two sticks, Judah and Joseph, as a sign that they will be one kingdom.

title: Gog and the Restored Temple
summary: The LORD tells Ezekiel to prophesy against Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, who will gather Persia, Ethiopia, Libya and others against a secure Israel. God will bring Gog down with earthquake, pestilence, hailstones and fire, and birds and beasts will feed on the slain. Israel will burn the weapons for seven years and bury the dead for seven months. In the twenty-fifth year of exile Ezekiel is set on a high mountain and sees a man with a measuring reed.
